proposals: DPIIT should publish a dated quarterly table for all PLI schemes showing approved outlay, claims received, claims paid and claims pending, by scheme and beneficiary, so the programme-wide disbursement rate — about 18% by March 2026 — need not be pieced together from scattered parliamentary answers.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries should name all ten manufacturers behind its “10 manufacturers, 178 GWh announced” battery figure, with each one's status under PLI-ACC, or drop the figure, since seven government documents repeat it while naming only the four approved cell-makers.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries and MNRE should report, beneficiary by beneficiary, the milestone each PLI-ACC and PLI Solar participant has or has not met, so the zero disbursement against more than ₹36,000 crore of combined outlay can be explained by the ministries rather than inferred.

The Department of Pharmaceuticals should publish a dated list of every applicant that has left PLI Medical Devices, with the reason, so the shrinkage of the approved list from 32 to 27 is formally recorded instead of discovered by comparing old and new rosters.

MeitY should publish beneficiary-wise PLI-LSEM disbursements each year, with the reason any approved beneficiary has received nothing, so readers can tell why 25 of 32 beneficiaries were at nil while payouts concentrated in two or three names.
